notes:
Follow mode interaction spec (ADR-005; design work in CHR-629; approved by Christian). The daemon derives one `activity` event per MCP tool call: `{ tool, kind: "read"|"write", target: {kind, name, variant?} | null, nodes: string[], ok, at }`.

**Follow toggle.** Per-browser preference, off by default. Three states: off · following · paused ("Follow paused | Resume"). In the real implementation this is ONE always-present control in the topbar, not a per-tab thing — the topbar's `follow`/`follow-paused` design-file variants are illustrative artefacts (two static states shown embedded in the Screens-tab layout, since this project's components can't parameterize a slot-filled instance by state), not a suggestion that the control forks per tab. Lives in the mode-button cluster, immediately before Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode — see `$follow-toggle`.

**Pause precedence** (highest wins):
1. The human wins. Any human navigation (clicking a different screen/tab/node), or an open comment/inspect mode, pauses follow — EXCEPT clicking a feed entry (see Feed below, changed by Christian's decision). Clearing the pausing condition does NOT auto-resume — only an explicit click on "Resume" (in the paused toggle) re-arms follow and jumps to the latest target.
2. An explicit agent presentation on the Board (the CHR-621 banner) also pauses follow.
3. Otherwise, follow.

**Navigation.** Targeted calls navigate: `get_screenshot`, `inspect_node`, `get_node`, `get_screen`, `get_mockup`, and all writes with a target. Broad reads (`get_project`, `find_nodes`, `get_design_system`, `list_comments`, `get_guide`) appear in the feed only, never navigate. Navigation is coalesced to at most once per 300ms.

**Highlight.**
- Read: solid 2px `$color.activity-read` (teal) outline, appears immediately, fades after **1.2s**.
- Write (node-level): 2px DASHED `$color.activity-write` (violet) outline + `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)` wash, appears only after the write's re-render lands, or after a **1s grace** if no re-render is observed, fades after **2.5s**.
- Write (whole-screen, after `write_html`): same violet, 3px dashed border around the entire screen frame + a small "Updated" pill badge at the top-right corner — never red, never an exclamation glyph, so it doesn't read as an error. Same 2.5s duration as node-level write.
- A `component:`/`pattern:` target navigates to the Design System view and highlights the node in its standalone-variant render, identical treatment.
- A mockup target (no node ids) gets navigation only, plus a transient cue on the relevant sidebar section (colored left border + faint wash, same read/write color) — no node box, since mockups have none.
- **Distinction from the two pre-existing highlights, verified against shipped code (`artisign/src/preview/style.css` `#inspect-overlay`, `artisign/src/preview/comments.js:13-14`):** the inspect overlay is `outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 1px; background: rgba(42,62,219,0.06)` — accent blue, solid. A selected comment target is `outline: 2px solid #d97706` (amber, solid); a comment marker (anchored but not selected) is `outline: 2px dashed #d97706` (amber, **dashed**). So dash pattern alone does NOT separate the write highlight from a comment marker — both are dashed. The separation is hue (violet vs. amber vs. accent blue) plus, for write specifically, the translucent wash and (whole-screen case) the "Updated" badge, which neither the inspect overlay nor comment outlines carry. Under protanopia/deuteranopia (red-green colorblindness, the common forms), blue-channel perception is largely intact, so violet's blue component should keep it distinguishable from blue-absent amber even when hue naming is unreliable; under full monochromacy the wash/badge are the only remaining cues.

**Feed.** Last **N = 50** calls, newest first, lives inside the existing right-side panel as a new "Activity" tab alongside "Elements" (`$panel-tabs`) — no new 1440px-wide column. Fills even when follow is off. In-memory, cleared on reload and on project switch. Each row (`$activity-entry`): tool name, target, relative time, ok/error. **Clicking an entry** with a live target navigates there exactly like a live tool call would (same highlight rules apply) — DECIDED by Christian: unlike every other human navigation, a feed click does NOT pause follow. It's exempt from precedence rule 1 — the human is still just watching the agent's own history, not designing something themselves, so the very next navigating agent call pulls the view straight back to the agent's live target. **Clicking a failed (`ok:false`) or deleted-target entry does nothing** — both render in a disabled look (dimmed / red-tinted-but-inert respectively, `cursor: default`) rather than a tooltip or toast; failed calls never navigate or highlight, by design, not as an oversight.

**Design-system view / mockup compare view.** Follow behaves identically in the Design System view (definition-target highlighting, see above) — no special case. Mockup compare view: navigation-only per the mockup rule above.

**Out of scope for CHR-629** (per ticket): the Board tab's own follow behavior, agent cursors/avatars, and implementation. See screens `follow-active-feed`, `follow-paused-node-highlights`, `follow-highlight-dark`, `follow-highlight-definition`, `follow-mockup-cue`, `follow-feed-empty`. New components: `$follow-toggle`, `$activity-entry`, `$activity-highlight` (reference-only, see its own usage notes), `$panel-tabs`. New tokens: `color.activity-read`, `color.activity-write`, `color.warning-subtle`.
